question: A dipole is placed in an electric field as shown. In which direction will it move ?
diagram_alt: Dipole with +q on the left and −q on the right in an electric field E whose lines spread out to the right

options.text: towards the right as its potential energy will increase.
towards the left as its potential energy will increase.
towards the right as its potential energy will decrease.
towards the left as its potential energy will decrease.

solution:
The field lines spread out to the right, so the field is non-uniform: stronger on the left and weaker on the right.

$+q$ is on the left, where the field is stronger, and is pushed right with force $qE_{\text{left}}$. $-q$ is on the right, where the field is weaker, and is pulled left with the smaller force $qE_{\text{right}}$. The net force is to the right.

Equivalently, $\vec{p}$ (from $-q$ to $+q$) points to the left, opposite to $\vec{E}$, so $U = -\vec{p}\cdot\vec{E} = +pE$. Moving right into the weaker field lowers $U$. The dipole moves to the right and its potential energy decreases.
